summary.oneLiner: Saint-Gobain Sekurit India Limited is a subsidiary of the Paris-headquartered Compagnie de Saint-Gobain that specializes in glass processing to manufacture windshields and other automotive glazing products for the Indian automotive industry.
summary.business: SGSIL operates within the Mobility (Sekurit) business of Saint-Gobain's High-Performance Solutions division, processing glass into windshields and other automotive glazing. Its Chakan (Pune) facility focuses exclusively on producing laminated automotive glass, which by law must be used for windshields, while rear and side windows use tempered glass. The Company sells to Original Equipment Manufacturers - passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles and three-wheelers - and into the more fragmented Replacement (aftermarket) segment, and recognizes Automotive Glass as a single segment.

currentContext.strengths: Considerable entry barriers in the sector, primarily due to the substantial capital investment required to establish advanced manufacturing and quality assurance infrastructure|Subsidiary of Compagnie de Saint-Gobain, a transnational group that reported sales of EUR 46.5 billion in 2025, with processes and controls aligned to Saint-Gobain Group best practices|Concentrated OEM competitive field - in the three-wheeler OEM category the Company faces competition from one major competitor and two other smaller entities|Quality and safety certifications (ISO 14001:2015, ISO 45001:2018, IATF 16949:2016) required to hold OEM contracts mandating just-in-time delivery and technical specification adherence|Emphasis on innovation and value-added products, enhanced service offerings and differentiated solutions to counter substitute materials and technology shifts
currentContext.strategies: Maintain a strategic emphasis on growing presence in the OEM segment, with targeted initiatives focused on the three-wheeler, truck, Light Commercial Vehicle (LCV), bus and aftermarket categories.|Capitalise on opportunities in the commercial vehicles market, enter the emerging Electric three-wheeler OEM segment, and expand within the small commercial vehicle sector.|Further accelerate the strategy addressing growth prospects in the bus body and LCV segments, which contributed positively last financial year.|Expand and strengthen the distribution network as a key priority to boost aftermarket growth.|Increase business with current customers, broaden value-added offerings in commercial vehicles, execute new light commercial vehicle programs, and expand further in the bus body market.|Prioritise innovation and development of value-added products tailored to shifting customer requirements, complemented by enhanced service offerings and differentiated solutions.|Optimise output across existing production lines through targeted automation initiatives that elevate product quality and consistency of output.|Drive sustainability by increasing the share of renewable energy across facilities, raising recycled content in packaging and strengthening cullet circularity (recovering and reusing glass in production).|In the Bus segment, pursue strategic marketing initiatives emphasising safety awareness and collaboration with bus body manufacturers to generate new business opportunities.|Continue aligning all processes and controls with Saint-Gobain Group's best practices; build a high-performance culture on Trust, Empowerment and Collaboration (TEC).
currentContext.expansion: The Board's Report describes no new plant or greenfield project. Expansion in FY2025-26 came from optimising output across existing production lines: with sustained demand for windshields providing a strong foundation, the Company made meaningful progress in improving production and delivery capabilities, and introduced a series of targeted automation initiatives that elevated product quality and enhanced the consistency and dependability of output. Manufacturing operations grew more resource-efficient, with measurable reductions in water and energy consumption per square meter of glass produced; the Company continued increasing the share of renewable energy across its facilities, raised the proportion of recycled content in its packaging, and strengthened cullet circularity (recovering and reusing glass in production). Forward-looking growth is framed as commercial rather than capacity-led - value-added glazing opportunities arising from mandatory air-conditioned cabins (supply to one key customer has started, with discussions ongoing with others), new light commercial vehicle programs, and further expansion in the bus body market. No material changes or commitments affecting the financial position of the Company occurred between the end of the financial year and the date of the Report.
currentContext.mdna: The Company enters FY2027 with a constructive outlook, backed by resilient structural tailwinds across India's automotive market and sustained momentum in both domestic and export channels.|The three-wheeler segment stands at an inflection point: after record-breaking FY2026 performance, it is set to enter a strategic 'reset phase' where growth moderates on the high base effect but the underlying trajectory remains firmly positive.|Electric three-wheelers are expected to be the defining growth catalyst of the next phase; electric three-wheelers already account for over 60% of retail sales in the segment and electrification is now the industry's new baseline.|In the commercial vehicle space, the post-upcycle environment of FY2027 is expected to yield moderate, consistent growth - a reflection of a maturing demand cycle rather than any structural headwind.|The aftermarket glass replacement industry is expected to see consistent growth, driven by the introduction of new references and better service within the Truck and Bus sectors.|Recovery of the Medium & Heavy Commercial Vehicle segment, which returned to positive growth after several difficult years; commercial vehicles were buoyed by stepped-up government infrastructure spending and improved financing access.|The introduction of mandatory air-conditioned cabins in Medium & Heavy Commercial Vehicles creates opportunities for value-added glazing; the Company has started supplying one key customer and is in discussions with others.|Regulatory developments are creating demand for products that enhance safety, comfort, weight reduction, sustainability and durability.|The Indian automotive market offers significant opportunities driven by higher volumes and increased demand for high-specification components; aftermarket potential is rising on stronger new vehicle sales, a broader distribution network and additional product references.|Ongoing digitalisation of the automotive industry, including connected vehicles and digital sales channels, is giving OEMs new avenues to improve customer experience and launch innovative products and services.|Performance is closely linked to cyclical trends and demand fluctuations inherent in the broader automotive industry; success is driven by product quality, cost efficiency, dependable supply for both OEMs and the aftermarket, and robust customer relationships.|Management is cautious about how evolving geopolitical tensions in West Asia may introduce unforeseen volatility into the future operating environment.

risks.risk: Automotive cyclicality — earnings tied to a single end-industry
risks.note: The MD&A states the Company's performance is closely linked to cyclical trends and demand fluctuations inherent in the broader automotive industry, and the Company recognizes Automotive Glass as a single segment, so there is no second business to offset a downturn.

BRSR Section A shows 100% of turnover from manufacture of laminated glass and one national plant with no other plants or offices (Chakan, Pune) — any disruption at that site or in that product line hits the whole revenue base.

risks.risk: Substitute materials, manufacturing-technology shifts and changing regulations
risks.note: The MD&A's Market Related Risks state that substitute materials, advancements in manufacturing technologies and changing regulations may impact product demand and could result in reduced market share; mitigation relies on innovation, value-added products and enhanced service offerings.

risks.risk: Volatile raw material and energy costs and supply-chain disruption
risks.note: Operational Risks flag volatile raw material and energy costs and potential supply chain disruptions that could impact production and business continuity; mitigation is diversifying the supplier base across geographies and establishing alternative sourcing.
The MD&A explicitly notes IT system failures pose a threat to manufacturing, and the People Risks section adds data security to the risks actively monitored.

risks.risk: Currency volatility, asset impairment and geopolitical exposure
risks.note: Financial Risks cite volatile global currency fluctuations and potential asset impairments, mitigated by systematic hedging of imports and exports; management is explicitly 'a bit cautious' of how evolving geopolitical tensions in West Asia may introduce unforeseen volatility into the future operating environment.

risks.risk: Stringent environmental regulation and compliance liability
risks.note: Regulatory Risks state that failure to comply with increasingly stringent environmental regulations could lead to substantial liabilities and reputational damage; the Company also monitors risks related to hazardous materials and environmental impact.

risks.risk: Talent, labour unrest and leadership continuity in a very small permanent workforce
risks.note: People Risks flag potential disruptions from labour unrest and the need for leadership continuity; the Company had 94 employees at year-end with 285 of 327 workers on third-party payroll or contract labour, and permanent-employee turnover of 14% in FY2025-26, while KMP turnover has been high (three different Whole Time Director/CFO appointments or resignations between July 2024 and May 2025).

risks.risk: OEM contract performance standards and customer concentration in a narrow competitive field
risks.note: OEM contracts mandate just-in-time delivery, technical specification adherence and quality certifications; in the three-wheeler OEM category the Company faces one major competitor and two smaller entities, and forward growth depends on 'one key customer' the Company has started supplying for AC-cabin glazing plus discussions with others.
